Subject: Load test coordination recap + next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get your customer-driven load test scheduled and make sure we validate the SLOs you called out.

Call highlights:
- Target latency SLOs: p95 <= 250ms for text-generation requests (avg prompt length ~350 tokens).
- Throughput target: sustained 120 qps, burst to 350 qps for short windows.
- Concurrency: concurrent sessions ~60 workers (streaming-enabled for live UI).
- Streaming: must support chunked responses with partial tokens and connection keep-alive; client will validate partial-token latency.
- Test tooling: Redbank prefers to drive the test using k6 for HTTP-level traffic, but open to Locust for more complex session-level flows.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We (Redwood) provide a k6 script + optional Locust file and a test account with scoped API keys.
2) Redbank validates IP allowlist and confirms test window (looking at Nov 9–10).
3) Shared Slack channel / short runbook for escalation during the window.

Action items from this thread:
- Marissa: attach k6 + locust artifacts and list of required IPs and ports.
- Logan: create test API key & test account, post placeholder credentials to the secure doc.
- Neha: confirm final window once Redbank replies.

Attachments: redwood_k6_script_v1.js (draft), redwood_locustfile_v1.py (draft), redwood-loadtest-checklist.pdf

Thanks — I’ll block the tentative window on our side but will wait for your confirmation before sending official invites.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — appreciate the recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we lock the window:

- The p95 target you noted looks right. We also need p99 <= 450ms for SLA gating.
- Streaming behavior: our UI will open a streaming connection and expect first token within 120ms for user-perceived latency checks. Can you confirm Redwood’s measured cold/steady-state first-token times (we discussed in the call but please send numbers)?
- IP allowlist: we will need the public egress IPs you’ll use for the region and any range that k6 cloud might hit.
- Test account: we will need a scoped API key that cannot access production customer data and a short-lived test org.

We’re aiming for Nov 9 (Tuesday) 10:00–14:00 EST for the main run, with a shorter smoke on Nov 8 if needed. Please confirm availability and send the script/checklist so our infra team can review tomorrow.

—Rajesh
Senior Engineering Manager, Redbank Financial

Hi Rajesh — looping in Aditya (runtime lead) and Logan (platform ops). Quick responses inline and attached materials.

- Measured latency: in our EU/US hosted configuration for the model variant we discussed (open-llama-13b-quant), typical steady-state first-token p50~60ms, p95~200ms, p99~380ms; cold-start (after idle > 3m) first token can be ~450–700ms depending on KV cache miss. We recommend priming traffic 10 minutes before the main run to avoid cold artifacts.

- p99 note: we can target p99 <= 450ms but please expect tail sensitivity during burst windows; we recommend rolling bursts (staggered worker ramp-ups) to hit peak concurrency without overwhelming autoscaling.

- Streaming: our streaming endpoints support chunked transfer; first token times above reflect our measured times for chunked responses. We’ll enable server-side keep-alive and monitor connection resets.

- IPs / allowlist: attached list is minimal egress ranges for the US region (redwood-egress-us-1: 34.82.10.0/24, 34.82.11.0/24) plus optional k6 cloud ranges. If you plan to run k6 from your own infra, only add the two ranges above. If you’ll use k6 cloud, we’ll share the k6 outbound ranges separately.

- Test account: Logan will create a test org and generate scoped API keys with the following constraints: no access to customer data, rate-limited to 500 qpm for the account, and keys will auto-expire in 7 days.

Attached: redwood_k6_script_v1.js (k6 scenario with ramp, sustained stages, and chunked streaming check), redwood_locustfile_v1.py (session-style locust file), redwood-loadtest-checklist.pdf (pre-test checklist).

Runbook / recommended windows:
- Nov 8 14:00–15:00 EST: smoke (connectivity, allowlist, basic latency checks)
- Nov 9 10:00–14:00 EST: main run (staged ramps to 120 qps sustained, bursts to 350 qps)

Operational contacts during test:
- Marissa Cole (runtime ops): marissa.cole@redwood.com
- Logan Wright (platform ops): logan.wright@redwood.com
- Aditya Rao (performance lead): aditya.rao@redwood.com

Please confirm the windows and whether you’ll run k6 from your infra or want to use k6 cloud. If k6 cloud, we’ll follow up with those IP ranges.
